solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strain's shown by husband and wife pursuing a people carrier

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the wife's letter comes after the A

parts.note: to rick is to strain or wrench a joint, so 'strain's' gives RICKS

explanation.surface: A tired couple strain as they chase after some sort of vehicle carrying passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'husband and wife' as a pair, but only the wife is 'pursuing a': H comes after RICKS, then A, then W.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled cart pulled by a runner or cyclist, it exists to carry passengers, hence a people carrier.

clue.text: Bang on front of residence by Jack had an impact

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here from residence

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman
bit, as in the cuts bit hard, means had an impact

explanation.surface: Jack's slamming of the front door made a real impression on the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on' is British slang for talking at tedious length, as is 'rabbit on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British idioms for chattering on and on, so rabbiting is going on boringly.

clue.text: Some Greek religious books with variable printed material?

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a bit of Greek
NT is the New Testament, a collection of religious books
Z is a letter used for an unknown variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Some Greek scriptures come in various printed editions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'printed material' suggests text, but the question mark points to fabric with a printed pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed cotton fabric printed with flowers, so it is literally printed material.

clue.text: Crime spot attracts local person of mystery

indicators.note: attracts means draws in, so the pub letters are pulled inside

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or crime
a local is a British pub, abbreviated PH for public house
X marks the spot on a map

explanation.surface: A crime scene draws in a local character who is something of an enigma.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub; maps mark a public house PH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphinx is an inscrutable person, after the riddling creature of Greek legend.

clue.text: Type of running track a centre of excellence with showers, for example

indicators.note: the centre of the ten-letter word excellence is its two middle letters

parts.note: showers are an example of weather

explanation.surface: An athletics venue boasts a top-class track and good showers for the athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showers' suggests changing rooms at a sports centre, but it is rain.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-weather track has a synthetic surface usable in any conditions, a kind of racing track.

clue.text: Metal container, earliest in trove, related to an ancient culture

indicators.note: the earliest letter in a word is its first one, so only the opening letter of trove is used

parts.note: Incan describes things belonging to the Inca civilisation of the Andes

explanation.surface: An archaeologist describes a metal box found first in a hoard, dating from Inca times.
explanation.definitionFit: A can made of tinplate is the everyday metal container for food and drink.

clue.text: Helpless monkey returned to hospital department

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the little word to is reversed

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A powerless little rascal is sent back to the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking power or strength, an impotent person is unable to act, so helpless.

clue.text: Perverse hoax attempt to apprehend artist

parts.note: a con is a hoax or swindle

indicators.note: to apprehend is to catch and hold, so the attempt word grips the artist

parts.note: a try is an attempt
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A con artist's attempt at deception is caught, which is a strange turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrary person is awkwardly opposed to whatever is wanted, which is perverse.

clue.text: The main card player's attending rehab regularly

parts.note: North is one of the four players in bridge, so card player's gives NORTHS

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every second letter of rehab

explanation.surface: The chief bridge player is going to rehab on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like 'the chief', but 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic name for the sea, and this sea lies off eastern Britain.

clue.text: Works in outskirts of biggish cathedral city, in a casual way

indicators.note: in places the works inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, the first and last of biggish

parts.note: LIT is short for literature, a body of written works
Ely is a small English city in Cambridgeshire known for its cathedral

explanation.surface: Building work on the edge of a fair-sized cathedral city goes ahead without much care.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means carefree or heedless, so the adverb describes doing something casually.

clue.text: During over with velocity excessive, confine batsman

indicators.note: during puts the confining word in the middle of what remains of over
excessive here means surplus, so the velocity letter is dropped from over

parts.note: taken as the word itself, OVER
V is the symbol for velocity in physics
to pen is to confine, as animals in an enclosure

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes that in one over the bowling was too fast to contain the batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a cricket over of six balls, but it is simply the word itself; 'excessive' marks the velocity letter as surplus, leaving OER for 'During' to hold the confine word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, an opening batsman is one of the pair who start the innings, commonly called an opener.

clue.text: At home, cycle together

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
a tandem is a bicycle built for two riders

explanation.surface: A couple at home decide to go out cycling as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting jointly or side by side, as riders on a two-seater bike work together.

clue.text: Before presentation of award, celebrity needs stiffener

indicators.note: before places the celebrity ahead of the award letters

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour awarded by the monarch

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes a stiff drink to steady the nerves before an awards ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, the Companion of Honour, is a British order conferred by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used in laundry to make collars and fabric rigid, so it is a stiffener.

clue.text: Retailer left in charge during transgression

indicators.note: during puts the two short abbreviations in the middle of the transgression word

parts.note: an offence is a transgression

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper on the left is held responsible for a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is a British shop selling alcohol to take away, like a liquor store.
explanation.definitionFit: This British shop sells drinks for consumption off the premises, so it is a retailer.

clue.text: Rod runs awkwardly, side of knee tender

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of runs are jumbled clumsily
a side of a word is an end; here the last letter of knee

explanation.surface: Someone running clumsily with a stick hurts the side of a knee, leaving it sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like an adjective about the knee, but it is the noun: one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a qualified hospital nurse, someone who tends patients, so a tender in the caring sense.

clue.text: Celebrity promoted second unaltered picture from 1970s

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, which in a down entry reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: raw means unprocessed or unaltered

explanation.surface: A famous actor is promoted, the second picture staying unchanged from the seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas's space-opera film appeared in 1977, so it is a motion picture from that decade.

clue.text: Tory politician good in speech, protesting angrily

indicators.note: in speech means the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to rail is to protest angrily, so railing

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP, generally decent, rants furiously while making a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Grayling is a British Conservative MP and former cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Grayling served in Conservative cabinets as transport secretary and justice secretary.

clue.text: Dine at sea, stimulating bile, and any food might seem thus

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of dine are jumbled
stimulating suggests stirring up, so the letters of bile are shaken about

explanation.surface: Eating on a rough sea voyage brings up bile, putting anyone off their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is unfit or unpleasant to eat is described as uneatable, which is how it seems to a seasick diner.

clue.text: See you, when in North America, count steps

parts.note: ta-ra is an informal British goodbye, like see you

indicators.note: in places the count word inside the abbreviation for North America

parts.note: to tell is an old sense of count, as a bank teller counts money

explanation.surface: A traveller says goodbye and, once in America, counts the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: TA-RA is a cheery northern English farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast Italian folk dance, a set of dance steps.

clue.text: Friend perhaps a bogus doctor, caught out by hesitant remark

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the caught letter leaves

parts.note: a quack is a fake doctor
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A pal might be a fraudulent medic, exposed after a stammering reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend' is a member of the Religious Society of Friends; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Religious Society of Friends call one another Friends, so a Friend is one example.

clue.text: It's a gemstone, according to past head of jewellery

indicators.note: past means beyond, so the according-to phrase comes after the head letter
the head of a word is its first letter, here from jewellery

parts.note: as per is a phrase meaning according to

explanation.surface: An expert pronounces a stone genuine, citing a former chief jeweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, often reddish variety of quartz used as an ornamental stone.

clue.text: Lift disheartening sermon at church

indicators.note: to dishearten here is to remove the heart, leaving the outer letters of sermon

explanation.surface: A dispiriting sermon at church could lift anyone's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' reads as gloomy, but it removes the middle of 'sermon'.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to steal or grab, a sense of lift; it is also a weightlifting move.

clue.text: During fourth day, Irene reviewed capital abroad

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again backwards
during points to letters running through the middle of the words fourth day, Irene

explanation.surface: Irene looked over her notes on the fourth day of a trip to a foreign capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters HDAYIR span the end of 'fourth', all of 'day' and the start of 'Irene'; 'reviewed' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia, so a capital in a foreign land.

clue.text: Son Colin peripherally embraces genial composer

indicators.note: embraces means the outer letters wrap around the genial word
peripherally means at the edges, so only the first and last letters of Colin

parts.note: human can mean kindly or sympathetic, as in a human touch

explanation.surface: A friendly composer gives Colin's son a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer of piano music and symphonies.

clue.text: Stance writer's taken after spirit rebuffed by book circle

indicators.note: taken after places the writer's letters following the turned-round spirit
rebuffed means pushed back, so the spirit word is turned round

parts.note: the ka is the soul or spirit in ancient Egyptian belief
the writer is I, so writer's means I am, shortened to I'M
O is a circle by shape

explanation.surface: A writer adopts a pose after a ghost is driven off by a book club.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'writer' can mean the setter, I; 'writer's' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo, with hands on hips and elbows out, describes a posture, so it stands for a stance.

clue.text: Wind pressure — it creates a site of mayhem

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road snakes through hills
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A gusting wind builds pressure and causes chaos somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a gale, but here it rhymes with 'kind': to meander.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake pit is figuratively any chaotic, dangerous scene, a place of turmoil and disorder.

clue.text: Soldier's rejected that woman who expresses dejection

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the soldier word is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, so soldier's gives GIS
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A soldier is turned down by a woman who is left downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: One who breathes out sadly, letting out a sigh, is expressing low spirits and dejection.

clue.text: Amended chapter includes right poet of Early Renaissance

indicators.note: includes means the rearranged letters take in the right letter
amended means altered, so the letters of chapter are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor revises a chapter on an Early Renaissance poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrarch was the fourteenth-century Italian poet of the sonnets to Laura, a founding Renaissance humanist.
